title: الكيمياء الحيوية
subtitle: Biochemistry
description: Oraby's Illustrated Reviews of Biochemistry — Q&A

lessons.title: Carbohydrate Chemistry
lessons.summary: Carbohydrates are polyhydroxy aldehydes or ketones. Monosaccharides are the simplest units. Disaccharides (sucrose, lactose, maltose) and polysaccharides (starch, glycogen, cellulose) are key forms. Glucose is the primary energy fuel.

lessons.title: Lipids Chemistry
lessons.summary: Lipids are hydrophobic biomolecules including fatty acids, triglycerides, phospholipids, and steroids. Saturated fats have no double bonds; unsaturated fats have one or more. Phospholipids form the cell membrane bilayer.

lessons.title: Amino Acids & Proteins
lessons.summary: 20 standard amino acids each with α-carbon, amino group, carboxyl group, and R-group. Proteins have 4 structure levels. Peptide bond links amino acids. 9 essential amino acids must come from diet.

lessons.title: Enzymes Chemistry
lessons.summary: Enzymes are biological catalysts (mostly proteins). They lower activation energy without being consumed. Key concepts: active site, Km, Vmax, competitive vs non-competitive inhibition, cofactors, coenzymes.

lessons.title: Nucleic Acids
lessons.summary: DNA stores genetic information; RNA expresses it. Nucleotides = nitrogenous base + pentose sugar + phosphate. DNA is a double-stranded antiparallel helix. RNA is single-stranded.

lessons.title: Vitamins
lessons.summary: Vitamins are essential organic micronutrients. Fat-soluble: A, D, E, K (stored in body fat). Water-soluble: B-complex, C (not stored, excreted in urine). Many B-vitamins act as coenzymes.
